To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the O6‐Alkylguanine‐ATase encoded by the O6‐GT gene enhances dibromoalkanes mutagenicity in Excision repair‐deficient E. Coli K‐12.
the alkyltransferases encoded by the o6‐alkyltransferase genes ogt and ada enhance dibromoalkane‐induced mutagenicity in bacteria.
the ogt gene product, O6‐alkyguanine‐DNA‐alkyltransferase (OGT), promotes dibromoalkane‐induced mutagenesis in excision repair‐defective bacteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of DNA‐repair systems in the mutagenicity of alkylating agents.
the study of the mutagenicity of alkylating agents and its modulation by DNA repair systems.

the study of the mutagenicity of dibromoethane (DBE), dibromomethanes (DBM), 2‐bromoethanol, and bromoform in bacteria and the role of DNA repair and mutagenic processing in the expression of their mutagenic potential.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(a) The ogt‐encoded ATase enhances the mutagenicity of dibromoalkanes in excision‐repair‐deficient bacteria; (b) the ogt‐encoded and the ada ATases are not equally effective in promoting mutagenicity of these compounds, the former being much more effective; and (c) the mutagenicity promoted is dependent on glutathione bioactivity and SOS mutagenesis.

the alkyltransferases are not involved in the repair of the alkylated DNA, and they do not protect the cells against the mutagenic and cytotoxic effects of alkylating agents.
